# BRAIN ABSCESS FROM CONTIGUOUS OR HEMATOGENOUS SPREAD OF INFECTION

Prior to beginning antimicrobial therapy, when possible, computed topographic (CT) - guided aspiration or surgery should be performed to obtain abscess material for determination of infectious pathogen. Adjust antimicrobial regimen to optimize therapy and treatment duration to optimize therapy based on pathogen once isolated.

Broad spectrum empiric antimicrobials are indicated initially for brain abscess. Staphylococcus aureus is a common pathogen. Beta-lactam antibiotics are more effective than vancomycin for susceptible Staphylococci. If Staphylococcus is isolated, once methicillin- resistance is ruled out, switch to an anti-staphylococcal beta-lactam antibiotic. Pseudomonas is a potential pathogen in post-surgical patients, and those who are known to be colonized with Pseudomonas.

# Consult Neurosurgery, Neurology, and Infectious Disease

## Empiric Treatment for Solitary Brain Abscess from Contiguous Source

Preferred:

Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q12h ($) [M] <AND> metronidazole 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) [DI]

Alternative:

Assessment of beta-lactam reaction

Meropenem 2 gm IV q8h ($$) R,O

## Empiric Treatment for Solitary Brain Abscess from Unknown Source, From

## Hematogenous Spread, Multiple Brain Abscesses or History of MRSA Infection or Colonization

Preferred if Pseudomonas is not likely:

Ceftriaxone 2 gm q12h ($) [M] <AND> metronidazole 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) [DI]
<AND> vancomycin 15mg/kg IV q12h ($) [R]

Preferred if Pseudomonas is likely:

Cefepime 2gm IV Q8h <AND> metronidazole 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) [DI] <AND> vancomycin 15mg/kg IV q12h ($) [R]

Alternative:

Assessment of beta-lactam reaction

Meropenem 2 gm IV q8h ($$) R,O  <AND> vancomycin 15mg/kg IV q12h ($) R
